messages:
Alex P: heads-up — got an inbound from enterprise-cust-42 about a p99 jump this morning in us-west. they reported ~400ms -> ~1.9s on text.generate calls. started ~08:12 UTC. request ids: req=R-97a3, trace=tx-0b4f.

Maya R: ugh. any recent changes to batching config or routing?

Alex P: we pushed a continuous-batcher tweak last night for better throughput (rollout 02:00 UTC): changed default `max_wait_ms` from 8 -> 50 and `min_batch_size` from 2 -> 4. intended to increase throughput for small-model traffic.

Jordan L: that sounds suspicious. longer max_wait will definitely blow up tail if arrival patterns are bursty. what percent of requests are small-token (<32) vs long?

Alex P: quick grab from metrics: p50 tokens ~12, p90 tokens ~48. small requests are ~62% of volume for this tenant.

Samir K: runbook says continuous-batcher safe defaults are `max_wait_ms` <= 20 for high small-request workloads. looks like this tenant should have been excluded from the rollout via per-tenant override.

Alex P: i pulled grafana panels — here's the chart snippet (link): https://grafana.redwood/boards/cont-batcher?from=2245003000&to=2245003600 — spike lines up with rollout.

Maya R: can you paste the relevant logs / tail for one of the slow request ids?

Alex P: log dump for req R-97a3: ```
2026-03-15T08:12:34.123Z INFO batcher: enqueued payload size=1 tokens=9 tenant=enterprise-cust-42
2026-03-15T08:12:34.174Z DEBUG batcher: hold-window elapsed=50ms batch_size=3 dispatching
2026-03-15T08:12:34.178Z INFO runtime: start-inference model=redwood-3b-quant
2026-03-15T08:12:34.200Z INFO runtime: first-token latency=20ms
2026-03-15T08:12:34.321Z INFO runtime: end-inference total=143ms
2026-03-15T08:12:34.324Z INFO http: response total=2010ms
```

Jordan L: that `hold-window elapsed=50ms` line explains it — client saw 2s end-to-end because batching wait + downstream queueing stack. also if many small single-token requests queue up, kernel startup overhead multiplies.

Samir K: immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback the `max_wait_ms` change globally, 2) add per-tenant override to set `max_wait_ms=8` for enterprise-cust-42, 3) enable `immediate_flush_on_small= true` for tenants with >50% small requests.

Maya R: what about scaling? could we increase batch workers for that shard to reduce queueing?

Alex P: scaling helps throughput but not the hold-induced tail — customers waiting for hold window still see extra ms. scaling might hide it partially by reducing time to hit min_batch_size, but arrival rate is low/bursty.

Samir K: agree — best short term is per-tenant override rollback. i've drafted a hotfix: `PATCH /admin/batcher-config/tenants/enterprise-cust-42 { "max_wait_ms": 8, "min_batch_size": 2 }`

Alex P: can you apply? i'm on-call and ready to monitor.

Samir K: applying now... :wrench: (deploy-bot) ```deployed config 2245003278 -> tenant enterprise-cust-42```

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: rollout complete for tenant enterprise-cust-42 (config id=2245003278)

Maya R: monitoring panels — p99 back down from 1.9s -> 230ms within 40s of the override. nice.

Jordan L: we should add a guard in the rollout workflow: if target traffic has >50% small requests, disallow `max_wait_ms` > 20. file a ticket?

Alex P: filed SRE-8932 with suggested policy and a short playbook for customer escalation. assigned to Samir.

Samir K: will also add an automated per-tenant sampling job to compute small-request ratio daily and flag risky rollouts.

Alex P: notes for post-incident: root cause = aggressive increase of continuous-batcher `max_wait_ms` in a global rollout without per-tenant risk gating. immediate fix = tenant-level rollback. follow-ups = policy guard + sampling job + runbook update. tagging support to notify customer. :memo:

Maya R: thanks — closing thread once support confirms customer is satisfied. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: incident annotated (id=INC-2245003300) — priority=high, status=mitigated, owner=Samir K

Alex P: support confirmed customer-sanctioned mitigation, customer saw normal p99 for the last 30m. marking resolved.
